title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?
abstract: arXiv:2610.29528v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Masked language modelling (MLM) is the dominant pretraining objective for transformer encoders applied to longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs). However, reconstructing individual events may overemphasise noisy or weakly informative observations and does not explicitly encourage learning higher-level patient states. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) instead learn by predicting representations in latent space and have shown strong performance in a variety of domains. In this paper, we investigate to what extent JEPA can be adapted to EHR sequence representation. Our empirical investigation using MIMIC-IV shows that although all three of our JEPA formulations train stably without representational collapse, they consistently underperform standard MLM. translated_title: 联合嵌入预测目标对纵向电子健康记录是否有效？
translated_abstract: 掩码语言建模（MLM）是目前应用于纵向电子健康记录（EHR）的Transformer编码器的主流预训练目标。然而，重建单个事件可能会过度强调含噪声或信息量较弱的观测，且并不能明确地促进模型学习更高层次的患者状态。联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）则通过在潜在空间中预测表示来进行学习，并已在多种领域展现出强大性能。本文研究了JEPA在多大程度上能够适配EHR序列表示。基于MIMIC-IV数据集的实证研究表明，尽管我们提出的三种JEPA公式都能稳定训练且不发生表示坍塌，但其表现始终不及标准MLM。我们发现，是预测目标的规模而非目标的异质性增加了预测误差，然而减小目标规模也无法恢复下游任务的性能。这表明……
tldr: 该研究表明，尽管JEPA方法在纵向电子健康记录的表示学习中能够稳定训练且不发生表示坍塌，但其性能始终不如标准的掩码语言建模，且减小预测目标规模也无法改善下游任务表现。
en_tdlr: Although JEPA formulations train stably without representational collapse on longitudinal EHRs, they consistently underperform standard masked language modeling, and reducing prediction target size fails to recover downstream performance.
